habitat: Dense thickets in riverine forest, at the base of densely wooded hills, and in termite mounds.
summary: A common localised resident. Deep orange underparts, with a black cap and mask set off by a bold white eyebrow. The immature is spotted. The song is a series of melodious phrases that build to a crescendo, mostly at dawn and dusk. The Kemp name Heuglin’s Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

head.pattern: Black cap and mask, with a bold white eyebrow.

viewNotes.note: Black cap and mask, a white eyebrow, and deep orange underparts.

calls.description: Melodious phrases repeated up to about 16 times, starting quietly and building. The grade A song is from near Hazyview. The filename is XC365336-Robin Chat Heuglins_Hazyview_150813_B_edit.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common localised resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The grade A song is from near Hazyview. The Kemp name Heuglin’s Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.
